accepted.s:
With reference to the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill, consider the following statements:
1. It was moved by the Rajiv Gandhi Government in the Lok Sabha in July 1989.
2. It sought to give constitutional status to Panchayats.
3. It was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989 for want of the required special majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in July 1989 by the Rajiv Gandhi Government, sought constitutional status for Panchayats, and was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989 because it did not secure the special majority.
accepted.tq: Use a statement-combination question to verify the proposal, date and legislative outcome together.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status attempts - 64th Amendment Bill, failure, origin of the 73rd

accepted.s: The principal objection raised by opponents to the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill was that it would
o: remove the system of reservation in local bodies
centralise power and bypass the States
accepted.x: Opponents feared that the 64th Bill would centralise power and bypass the States in matters relating to Panchayati Raj.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific political objection rather than the broad objective of the Bill.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status attempts - 64th Amendment Bill, failure, origin of the 73rd

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional-status initiative during the V.P. Singh Government?
o: The Bill was converted directly into the 73rd Amendment Act in 1990.
The Bill was passed by both Houses but later rejected by the President.
The Bill was withdrawn after the adoption of the 64th Amendment Act.
A fresh Bill was introduced in 1990 but lapsed when the Government fell.
accepted.x: The V.P. Singh Government introduced a fresh Bill in 1990, but it lapsed when the Government fell.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘true start, false end’ trap to distinguish introduction from enactment.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status attempts - 64th Amendment Bill, failure, origin of the 73rd

accepted.s:
Consider the following developments:
A. Introduction of a fresh Panchayati Raj Bill by the V.P. Singh Government
B. Passage of the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha
C. Coming into force of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment
D. Defeat of the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill in the Rajya Sabha
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
accepted.x: The 64th Bill passed the Lok Sabha in July 1989, was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in October 1989, a fresh Bill followed in 1990, and the 73rd Amendment came into force in 1993.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events before arranging the intervening legislative developments.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status attempts - 64th Amendment Bill, failure, origin of the 73rd

accepted.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 emerged after the controversial portions of the earlier proposal were dropped during the tenure of
accepted.x: The P.V. Narasimha Rao Government during 1991–92 dropped the controversial portions and enacted the revised proposal as the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the governments associated with the successive stages of one reform.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status attempts - 64th Amendment Bill, failure, origin of the 73rd

accepted.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 came into force on
accepted.x: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 came into force on 24 April 1993.
accepted.tq: Test the exact commencement date against closely spaced constitutional dates.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status attempts - 64th Amendment Bill, failure, origin of the 73rd

accepted.s:
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment was influenced by the recommendations associated with which of the following groups?
1. Singhvi
2. Thungon
3. Gadgil
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil lines of thinking contributed to the 73rd Amendment, particularly in relation to constitutional status, regular elections and reservation.
accepted.tq: Use an inclusive option when all three named recommendation streams form the correct group.
accepted.sec: Constitutional status attempts - 64th Amendment Bill, failure, origin of the 73rd

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Milestone)
A. Lord Mayo's Resolution
B. Lord Ripon's Resolution
C. Royal Commission on Decentralisation
D. Government of India Act, 1919

List-II (Significance)
1. Local self-government became a transferred provincial subject
2. Financial decentralisation
3. Stress on village panchayats
4. Magna Carta of local self-government

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Mayo's Resolution dealt with financial decentralisation; Ripon's Resolution was regarded as the Magna Carta of local self-government; the 1907 Royal Commission stressed village panchayats; and the 1919 Act made local self-government a transferred provincial subject.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair ‘Ripon–Magna Carta’ and eliminate incompatible codes.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence local self-government - Mayo, Ripon, Royal Commission

accepted.s: The Royal Commission on Decentralisation, appointed in 1907, was associated with which of the following persons?
accepted.x: The Royal Commission on Decentralisation, appointed in 1907 and reporting in 1909, was associated with Hobhouse and stressed the importance of village panchayats.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the person associated with the commission from the persons associated with earlier resolutions.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence local self-government - Mayo, Ripon, Royal Commission

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Panchayati Raj laws is correct?
o: The AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959 introduced the three-tier structure in the State.
The AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 abolished the Mandal Parishad tier.
The AP Gram Panchayats Act was enacted in 1959 to replace Zilla Parishads.
The AP Mandal Praja Parishads Act was enacted by the Government of P.V. Narasimha Rao in 1991.
accepted.x: The AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959 brought in the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-authority and wrong-year traps to separate the major Andhra Pradesh laws.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayati Raj laws and the Mandal Praja Parishad reform

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Mandal Praja Parishads reform of 1986 primarily aimed to
o: transfer all Panchayat functions to municipalities
replace smaller Mandal Praja Parishads with larger district bodies
replace block Panchayat Samithis with smaller Mandal Praja Parishads
accepted.x: The 1986 reform under the NTR Government replaced block-level Panchayat Samithis with smaller Mandal Praja Parishads, reflecting the mandal idea associated with the Ashok Mehta approach.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional reform to identify which tier was replaced and by what.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayati Raj laws and the Mandal Praja Parishad reform

accepted.s:
With reference to the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, consider the following statements:
1. It is Act 13 of 1994.
2. It was enacted on 21 April 1994.
3. It contains 278 sections and 8 Parts.
4. Its three tiers are Gram Panchayat, Mandal Parishad and Zilla Parishad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 is Act 13 of 1994, dated 21 April 1994. It contains 278 sections and 8 Parts and provides for Gram Panchayat, Mandal Parishad and Zilla Parishad tiers.
accepted.tq: Check the exact statutory number, date, structure and numerical details as one integrated set.
accepted.sec: AP Panchayati Raj laws and the Mandal Praja Parishad reform

accepted.x: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee reviewed both the Community Development Programme and the National Extension Service in January 1957.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rural development programmes in chronological order:
A. Integrated Rural Development Programme
B. National Extension Service
C. Community Development Programme
D. National Adult Education Programme
accepted.x: The Community Development Programme began in 1952, the National Extension Service in 1953, the National Adult Education Programme in 1978, and the Integrated Rural Development Programme began in 1978–79 before its nationwide expansion in 1980.
accepted.tq: Fix the two early programmes first and then distinguish the 1978 adult-education and rural-development initiatives.
accepted.sec: Rural programmes in chronological order

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Food for Work programme is associated with 1977. ICDS was listed as 1975, TRYSEM as 1979 and DWCRA as 1982.
accepted.tq: Use nearby programme years as distractors and verify the exact programme-year association.
accepted.sec: Rural programmes in chronological order

accepted.s: The Integrated Area Development Programme (IADP) was initially introduced as a pilot project in
accepted.x: The IADP was introduced as a pilot programme in seven districts.
accepted.tq: Test the small numerical detail that is easily confused with later programme coverage.
accepted.sec: Rural programmes in chronological order

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the social education programme under the Community Development Programme?
accepted.x: Social education under the Community Development Programme included adult literacy, community centres, and youth and women's clubs. Industrial export promotion was not one of its components.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider by matching the options against the stated social-education activities.
accepted.sec: Social education component - its programme

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Social education was a component of the Community Development Programme.
2. Social education included adult literacy and community centres.
3. Social education was specifically a component of the National Adult Education Programme rather than the Community Development Programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the social education component described here belonged to the Community Development Programme, not to the National Adult Education Programme.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related adult-education terminology and the programme to which it belonged.
accepted.sec: Social education component - its programme

Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Person)
A. S.K. Dey
B. Albert Mayer
C. V.T. Krishnamachari
D. Jawaharlal Nehru

List-II (Association)

2. Built Nilokheri and served as Union Minister of Community Development
3. American planner behind the Etawah Pilot Project
4. Launched the Community Development Programme and inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: S.K. Dey was associated with Nilokheri and the Union Ministry of Community Development; Albert Mayer with the Etawah Pilot Project; V.T. Krishnamachari chaired the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee; and Jawaharlal Nehru launched the CDP and inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive associations ‘Mayer–Etawah’ and ‘Krishnamachari–Grow More Food’ to establish the code.

accepted.x: Albert Mayer was the American planner behind the Etawah Pilot Project.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the international technical adviser from Indian administrators and political leaders.

accepted.s: Which one of the following persons was associated with both the launch of the Community Development Programme in 1952 and the inauguration of Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru launched the Community Development Programme in 1952 and inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959.
accepted.tq: Connect two separate institutional milestones through the common political figure.
